artworks.title: Heracles and Linus
artworks.description: Attic red-figure kylix: young Heracles turns on his music-master Linus with the stool or lyre that will kill him. The cup is the clearest archaic image of the Thracian (or Theban) Linus — brother of Orpheus in some genealogies — whose pedagogy ends in the hero’s rage.

artworks.title: Herakles and Linos
artworks.description: Boston MFA stamnos 66.206: Heracles and Linos locked in the music-lesson murder that Apollodorus and later mythographers retell. Museum clay keeps the singing-master distinct from Pope Linus — a mythic death, not a papal name.

popCulture.title: Bibliotheca (Heracles and Linus)
popCulture.creator: Apollodorus
popCulture.description: Apollodorus records how Heracles killed his music-teacher Linus with the lyre — the handbook version of the death that Attic vases paint, keeping the Orphic brother distinct from later Christian namesakes.
